explanation: Mark each prefix that can be split into dictionary words, remembering where its last word starts. A reachable final prefix yields a decomposition by following those predecessor positions backward. Return an empty list when the final prefix is unreachable.
timeComplexity: O(n^3) worst-case time including substring copying and hashing.
spaceComplexity: O(n) auxiliary space, plus O(n) characters in the output.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract.
correctness: previous[end] is set only when a reachable earlier prefix is followed by a dictionary word. By induction, every marked prefix has a valid decomposition, and every valid decomposition marks its successive word boundaries. Following predecessors from the final boundary reconstructs one complete decomposition.
walkthrough: For "sunleaf" and {"sun","leaf","sunl"}, prefix "sun" becomes reachable at 3 and "sunl" at 4. Only the split after 3 can finish with dictionary word "leaf", so reconstruct ["sun","leaf"].
edgeCases: Return an empty list when no decomposition exists.
A dictionary word may be used repeatedly.
Any valid word sequence is accepted; do not require a single predetermined split.
